title: Learner 01 | Day 023: Composition, inheritance, and protocols
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ## Question of the Day
> Why use a context manager for file access?

## Goal

Make Tracker use a storage object exposing load and save; provide an in-memory storage implementation.

## Learn this first

Composition gives an object a collaborator. Inheritance specializes behavior; a protocol describes required operations without forcing a parent class.

<details><summary>Learn before coding: run this project-related example</summary>

```python
class StudySession:
    def __init__(self, minutes):
        self.minutes = minutes
    @classmethod
    def from_minutes(cls, minutes):
        return cls(minutes)
class FocusedSession(StudySession):
    pass
result = FocusedSession.from_minutes(15)
print(type(result).__name__, result.minutes)
```

Expected output:

```text
FocusedSession 15
```

An instance method receives its object as self. A class method receives the class used for the call as cls. Here cls is FocusedSession, so cls(minutes) creates that subclass and its instance receives minutes=15. pass adds no new behavior. Compare this with hard-coding StudySession(minutes), which would lose the subclass construction. Apply an alternate constructor only when your project model needs one; composition still keeps unrelated capabilities separate.

In review, execute the learner's actual code and trace each relevant line: purpose, name/object/attribute before and after, why, and its project contribution. Use a changed input or call order; do not claim a predicted run was executed.
</details>

## Method signature and expected behavior

**File:** `src/learnforge/adapters/connections/session_models.py`

**Function/class/value to change:** `handle_storage_contract`

**Why here:** This translates an external representation or service: raw input, HTTP/provider/protocol behavior, and error translation belong outside the core.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Tracker works with the fake store and does not import file-storage details.

**Boundaries:** Own parsing/transport only; delegate domain decisions and storage.

1. Research **Composition, inheritance, and protocols**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org Composition inheritance and protocols`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
